title: Support agents resolved more issues per hour
date_precision: The principal rollout occurred in fall 2020 and winter 2021. A single intervention date does not describe the staggered introduction.
location: Offices mainly in the Philippines, with smaller groups in the United States and other unnamed countries
system: Unnamed customer-support assistant built on GPT-3
observed_outcome: Access to an AI assistant increased resolved customer issues per hour by about 15% on average in one software company.
ai_contribution: Suggested replies and relevant internal documentation during customer chats.
human_contribution: Agents diagnosed problems, chose whether to use or edit suggestions, and remained responsible for replies. Managers continued coaching.
evidence_supports: A difference-in-differences analysis of deployment across 5,172 agents estimates 0.301 additional resolutions per hour, or 15.2%, in the preferred model. That model uses 12,295 agent-month observations with the required outcome data.
limitations: One firm and a nonrandomized rollout. Causal interpretation depends on the comparison assumptions. Quality measures were unavailable for some subcontracted agents. Gains varied by experience and skill. Wages and economy-wide employment effects were not measured.
tradeoffs: The most skilled agents saw a small decline in conversation quality. The average customer satisfaction effect was not statistically significant.
replication_hypothesis: The observed setting combined company-specific training data, internal documentation, trained agents, and human discretion. Their separate contributions were not isolated.
beneficiaries: Customer-support agents and the employer. Productivity gains were concentrated among less experienced and lower-skilled agents.
stakeholder_detail: The full study covers 5,172 agents and 3,006,395 chats. It does not show that every worker benefited or establish higher pay.

sources.title: Generative AI at Work
sources.authors: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, and Lindsey Raymond

source_case_identifier: Preferred resolutions-per-hour estimate, Table II, column 3

evidence_basis.evidence_design: Difference-in-differences and event-study analyses of staggered individual access.
evidence_basis.reported_by: Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond in The Quarterly Journal of Economics
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: Firm records provide chat outcomes. Table II reports an adjusted increase in resolutions per hour. The main model controls for calendar month, agent, location, and tenure.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: Primary publication reviewed. This is a single-firm observational deployment study, not a randomized trial or an independently replicated result.

ai_attribution: The estimate concerns access to this company-specific assistant under the rollout conditions. It does not isolate the base model from training, documentation, and workflow.
editorial_classification_note: Use the final QJE estimate and sample. Do not substitute the earlier working-paper headline or interpret measured productivity as wage growth.

system_details.provider: Unnamed AI vendor using OpenAI GPT-3
system_details.source_note: Section III.C identifies GPT-3 fine-tuned on customer conversations. The company, vendor, exact model snapshot, and software release are not disclosed.

reporting_period.display: Main rollout in fall 2020 and winter 2021

denominators.notes: The resolutions-per-hour outcome is observed for a subset. Agent-month observations are not distinct people.

measurements.source_locator: Table II, column 3 and Section V.A

research_data.duration_follow_up: Repeated workplace observations around rollout. No estimate of long-run economy-wide effects.
limitations: Gains are heterogeneous and do not establish wage gains.
research_data.source_notes: Final journal version published February 4, 2025. Table I supplies sample counts. Sections III and IV supply system, geography, and rollout details.
research_data.evidence_status: Primary peer-reviewed publication reviewed. Independent replication is not established.

source_checks.claim: GPT-3, company-specific fine-tuning, suggestions and documentation links, and agent discretion
Philippines and United States named as agent locations
Fall 2020 and winter 2021 rollout and three-hour onboarding
Quality outcomes missing for some agents and no measured wage effects

documented_conditions: The model was fine-tuned on recorded support conversations labeled by outcomes, with greater weight on high performers.
The assistant supplied response suggestions and links to the company’s internal technical documentation.
Agents completed a three-hour onboarding session and could ignore or edit suggestions.
evidence_details.transfer_limit: A company-specific customer-support deployment does not establish the same gain for generic chatbots, other occupations, or workers with different experience.

related.reason: Both examine language assistance for professional communication and report larger gains among initially weaker performers.
related.caution: Customer support used live company workflows and a specialized GPT-3 system. The writing experiment used short tasks and general-purpose ChatGPT. Their percentages are not interchangeable.

evidence_details.comparison_short: Agents before access and agents without access during rollout.
